## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types

- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist

- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator

- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. # Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

#### The last failure per target

The registry remembers the last failure of each target, so a view can show it
after the run that produced it was pruned or the view was rebuilt. It lives in
`internal/jobs/failure.go` and `registry.go`.

**The key** is `FailureKey{Kind, Target, Context}`: the run's kind, `TargetKey(item.Target)`,
and `Run.Context`. One entry per key; a new failure for a key replaces the old one
and moves it to the newest position. A failure that lands after a context switch
is filed under the context it ran in, not the current one. `Item.Target` itself
is not rewritten; only the key is normalized.

**`TargetKey` cleans absolute paths and nothing else** (`filepath.Clean`). Image
references, forge paths and slugs are kept raw, because two spellings are not
provably the same target:

- `nginx` and `docker.io/library/nginx` are different keys: only the registry
  knows they resolve alike, and the memory does not ask it;
- an image is not a repository: a failure on `nginx` never shows on a repo of the
  same name, and the other way round (the kind is part of the key too).

**Transitions** are decided in one place, `Registry.record`, called from `Advance`
and `Discover`:

| Event | Effect |
|---|---|
| item `failed` | poses the failure (`Display`, `Detail`, `At`) |
| item `done` | clears the key |
| `Start` / `Discover` admitting a target | clears the key: a new attempt replaces the last word |
| `delete` item `done` | clears the target for every kind, and its descendants when it is an absolute path |
| item `skipped`, `Cancel` | nothing: a refusal or a stop is not a failure |
| `ForgetTargetMsg` | same as a done delete, for a removal no run did (an image remove) |

`ForgetTargetMsg` is stamped with the **current** context by the router
(`handleForgetTarget`); it never touches another context's failures, and
broadcasts only when something went. Descendants are matched on path only: a
non-absolute target is matched exactly.

**Bounds.** At most `MaxFailures` (500) entries; the oldest goes first. They are
independent of `MaxFinishedRuns`: pruning a settled run keeps its failures. The
memory lives for the process and is never written to disk. `Kind.Remembered()`
exists as the one place a policy could narrow this, and today every kind is
remembered, `index` included.

**Reading.** `ChangedMsg.Failures` carries a copy, oldest first, every context
included, like `Runs`. The view filters: `jobs.FailuresOn(failures, context, target, kinds...)`
returns what is on a target, and `jobs.FailureFor(failures, kind, target, context)`
one entry. Which kinds a view shows (D5) is the reader's choice, passed as `kinds`;
the registry keeps all of them.

**`ChangedMsg.Context`** (DEVDESK-145) is the router's current context when the
snapshot is sent, stamped in `changedMsg()` (`internal/app/jobs.go`), the only
builder. A view reads `Runs` and `Failures` against it, so it needs no
constructor argument: `:sec` stores it in `handleJobsChanged`. An unfed view has
an empty context, which matches no run. `ws` and `:jobs` still take the name as a
constructor argument (same value).

`security.scanTarget.Failed` was one of the two manual copies this replaces; it
was removed by DEVDESK-145 (A-08), and `:sec` reads `Failures` (scan kind only).
OCI's `failedScans` was the other; DEVDESK-146 (A-09a) removed it, and the
Images table reads `Failures` too (scan and pull kinds).

### A progress message needs a case in the router

### The `:jobs` view — `internal/ui/jobsview`

The reader's side of the registry, and it owns nothing: it starts no work, holds
no timer and fetches nothing. Its rows are the snapshot, so there is nothing to
refresh — `ctrl+r` is absent rather than greyed, because there is no operation
behind it to be unavailable.

Two levels (D2): the runs, and `→` on one of them for its targets. A level
rather than a pair of tabs — the second table is *about* a row of the first, so
it is reached the way every drill-down in the application is (Rule 111), and the
trail is a breadcrumb below the table (Rule 123).

| | Columns |
|---|---|
| runs | activity indicator (untitled, `IconColumnWidth`), Kind, Label, Progress, State, Started |
| targets | activity indicator, Target, State, Detail |

**Column 0 is the activity indicator** (DEVDESK-142, Rule 125), built by
`datatable.IndicatorColumn` over `components.RunIndicator` / `ItemIndicator`
(`job_activity.go`): queued `◴`, running `●`/`○`, done `◉`, failed `⊗`,
cancelled `⊘`, skipped `⊖`. It is the state, not the kind: a jobs list is
scanned for the run that failed and the one still going. The Kind column
carries the state in its `Search` so `/failed` and `/scan` both work while the
glyph column stays out of the filter. The State word takes the dot's colour
(`indicator.Style`), so the row has one colour source; `done` is neutral, not
green, and queued, cancelled and skipped now share that neutral colour.

**The blink phase is read at render.** The rows carry nothing animated:
`runRow`/`itemRow` wrap the record only. `jobs.FrameMsg` calls
`SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` on both tables and pushes the footer spinner frame;
no row is rebuilt (`SetItems` stays the only way rows are rebuilt, from
`ChangedMsg`). A queued run no longer spins: it shows a fixed `◴`.

**The footer says the selected row.** `status()` fills `Status.Detail` with
`components.DescribeRun` (or `DescribeItem` at the target level) of the row
under the cursor, and keeps `N jobs running` as the text. The footer spinner is
shown only when no detail is, since the row's own dot moves. A `Warn` (a refused
`K` or `.`) keeps priority over the detail and the detail returns when it
expires. The help ends with `indicator.Legend(indicator.JobsLegend...)`.

**The context is passed, not read.** `jobsview.New(cfg, contextName)` takes the
name from the router, for D68's reason one screen over: the router is what knows
which context is current. The view filters the snapshot on it (`FilterContext`),
so a switch hides runs rather than dropping them — and the router rebuilds every
view on a switch anyway, so the cached name cannot go stale.

`K` is state-aware at both levels (Rule 130) and greyed with a **named** reason:
"This run has already finished", "A delete cannot be stopped once it has
started". The refusal is never silent — pressing a greyed key says why in the
footer.

**The dashboard gained the counter** the same way, and it is the one screen that
always gets D9's degraded form: it launches nothing, so it passes no origin, and
`2 jobs running — :jobs for details` is the whole of what it can honestly say.
The sentence itself is `components.JobsStatusLine`, shared with the workspaces
footer — two copies of a deliberate surrender would each have been free to
surrender differently.

### Handing the terminal to a child — `internal/ui/teaexec`

85:| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |

51:When the terminal reports that it lost the focus (xterm mode 1004), the router stops the animation tick and tells the view on screen with a `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`. That view skips its periodic reads: the dashboard, `:oci`, `:containers`, the Ports tab and `:agent-usage` (whose header then reads `Updates › paused (terminal not focused)`). When the focus returns, each view reads once and the animation restarts. Jobs are never paused. 115:### The jobs registry — `internal/jobs`
117:A single, router-owned bookkeeping structure for everything long-running (`App.jobs`). It replaced four separate, mutually invisible tracking mechanisms scattered across views — which meant a scan started from the security view was invisible to the "is anything running" check in the workspaces view, and the two ended up racing to write the same cache entry.
132:**Open runs.** Most launches know their full target list up front, which is what lets the UI say "8 waiting". Cloning doesn't — discovering which repositories exist *is* the slow part — so `jobs.NewOpenRun` registers a run with no targets yet, and `Discover`/`Seal`/`CancelOpen` add targets as the walk finds them and eventually close it off. An open run is never considered "finished" just because its current items are — only an explicit seal closes it.
138:Views never hold a pointer into the registry. The router hands out a read-only snapshot via `jobs.ChangedMsg`, broadcast to every held view (on screen or not) whenever anything changes — so navigating back to a view that missed some progress shows the current state without it having to ask. `tea.View.ProgressBar` (OSC 9;4), so the terminal's tab or taskbar shows the work
the jobs registry holds. `jobs.Summarize` (`internal/jobs/progress.go`, pure: no
clock, no registry) reduces runs and failures to a `jobs.Progress`;
`terminalProgress` (`internal/app/terminal_progress.go`) maps it to a
`*tea.ProgressBar`.

- *Scope.* Only the current context (D8): `summarizeJobs` filters runs and
  failures with `jobs.FilterContext` / `jobs.FailuresIn`, and only unfinished runs
  count. Failures of the `index` kind count like any other (`:jobs` lists them), so
  an offline start turns the tab red until `:jobs` is shown once.
- *Precedence* (strongest first, the order of Rule 128):

  | Condition | `Progress.State` | `tea.ProgressBar` |
  |---|---|---|
  | a failure with `Seq` above the read mark | `ProgressError` | `{Error, 100}` |
  | an unfinished run is `Cancelled()` | `ProgressWarning` | `{Warning, Percent}` when measured, else `{Warning, 100}` |
  | unfinished runs, all measured | `ProgressPercent` | `{Default, Percent}` |
  | unfinished runs, at least one not measured | `ProgressIndeterminate` | `{Indeterminate, 0}` |
  | nothing | `ProgressIdle` | `nil`: the bar is cleared |

  A run is *measured* when it is sealed (not open) and holds at least two targets
  (`measurable`): an open run has no total yet, and a one-target run has no
  halfway. `Percent` is `100 * sum(Done) / sum(Total)` over all unfinished runs
  (integer division, so it floors). There is no persistent green bar (Rule 125):
  idle is `nil`. Error and Warning are drawn full so the state is the message and
  the bar stays visible on terminals that hide a 0 value; the 100 is untested on
  real terminals (see below).
- *Acknowledgement.* A failure is "read" once `:jobs` is on screen. `Failure.Seq`
  is a registry-assigned, strictly increasing number (see "The last failure per
  target"). The router keeps one watermark per context
  (`App.failuresReadThrough`); `summarizeJobs` raises it to
  `jobs.LatestFailureSeq` while `currentView == command.ViewJobs`. Failures with a
  higher `Seq` are unread. The failures stay listed in `:jobs`; only the bar goes
  back. A new failure for the same target gets a new `Seq`, so it turns the bar
  red again. The watermark lives in the process, per context, and is not written
  to disk.
- *When it is computed.* `broadcastJobs` calls `summarizeJobs` (from `Update`
  only, Rule 110). `syncTerminalProgress`, run after every `Update`, is a level
  check: it re-summarizes only when the context changed or when `:jobs` is on
  screen with an unread failure, whatever path brought the view in. Otherwise a
  tick copies no snapshot. `View()` reads the stored `a.progress` and does no work.
- *One owner.* Only `internal/app/view.go` assigns `ProgressBar`
  (`TestOnlyTheRouterSetsTheTerminalProgress`), and only `terminal_progress.go`
  builds a `tea.ProgressBar` (`TestOnlyTerminalProgressBuildsAProgressBar`): a
  second source would overwrite the first on the next frame.

  call. The renderer keeps the pointer it last drew and compares through it, so a
  bar mutated in place would look unchanged and never be redrawn
  (`TestViewHandsOutAFreshProgressBarEveryCall`). The renderer writes OSC 9;4 only
  when the value changes, not per frame.
- *Exit and `tea.ExecProcess`.* Bubble Tea 2.1.1 resets the bar (OSC 9;4;0) on
  close, on the same paths as the background reset, and around an exec; it sends
  the bar again when the renderer restarts. DevDesk adds nothing. Exec still goes
  through `internal/ui/teaexec`.
- *Degradation.* A terminal without OSC 9;4 ignores the sequence, and there is no
  way to detect that, so DevDesk does not try. There is no config key to turn the
  bar off (a future `app.terminal_progress: off` is a separate story if a terminal
  is found that prints the sequence). tmux needs `allow-passthrough` to forward it.

  `Failed N` (the context's remembered failures), the footer appends
  `· M stopping` to `N jobs running`, and the help has a "Terminal tab" section.

- *Limits.* Nothing resets the bar after `kill -9`, a panic in a goroutine that is
  not a `Cmd`, or a closed terminal: run `printf '\\e]9;4;0\\a'` to clear it.

the jobs registry holds. `jobs.Summarize` (`internal/jobs/progress.go`, pure: no

`terminalProgress` (`internal/app/terminal_progress.go`) maps it to a

  failures with `jobs.FilterContext` / `jobs.FailuresIn`, and only unfinished runs
  count. Failures of the `index` kind count like any other (`:jobs` lists them), so
  an offline start turns the tab red until `:jobs` is shown once.
- *Precedence* (strongest first, the order of Rule 128):

  | Condition | `Progress.State` | `tea.ProgressBar` |
  |---|---|---|
  | a failure with `Seq` above the read mark | `ProgressError` | `{Error, 100}` |
  | an unfinished run is `Cancelled()` | `ProgressWarning` | `{Warning, Percent}` when measured, else `{Warning, 100}` |

  (`measurable`): an open run has no total yet, and a one-target run has no
  halfway. `Percent` is `100 * sum(Done) / sum(Total)` over all unfinished runs
  (integer division, so it floors). There is no persistent green bar (Rule 125):
  idle is `nil`. Error and Warning are drawn full so the state is the message and
  the bar stays visible on terminals that hide a 0 value; the 100 is untested on
  real terminals (see below).

  is a registry-assigned, strictly increasing number (see "The last failure per
  target"). The router keeps one watermark per context
  (`App.failuresReadThrough`); `summarizeJobs` raises it to
  `jobs.LatestFailureSeq` while `currentView == command.ViewJobs`. Failures with a
  higher `Seq` are unread. The failures stay listed in `:jobs`; only the bar goes
  back. A new failure for the same target gets a new `Seq`, so it turns the bar
  red again. The watermark lives in the process, per context, and is not written
  to disk.
- *When it is computed.* `broadcastJobs` calls `summarizeJobs` (from `Update`
  only, Rule 110). `syncTerminalProgress`, run after every `Update`, is a level
  check: it re-summarizes only when the context changed or when `:jobs` is on
  screen with an unread failure, whatever path brought the view in. Otherwise a
  tick copies no snapshot. `View()` reads the stored `a.progress` and does no work.
- *One owner.* Only `internal/app/view.go` assigns `ProgressBar`
  (`TestOnlyTheRouterSetsTheTerminalProgress`), and only `terminal_progress.go`
  builds a `tea.ProgressBar` (`TestOnlyTerminalProgressBuildsAProgressBar`): a
  second source would overwrite the first on the next frame.

  call. The renderer keeps the pointer it last drew and compares through it, so a
  bar mutated in place would look unchanged and never be redrawn
  (`TestViewHandsOutAFreshProgressBarEveryCall`). The renderer writes OSC 9;4 only
  when the value changes, not per frame.

  close, on the same paths as the background reset, and around an exec; it sends
  the bar again when the renderer restarts. DevDesk adds nothing. Exec still goes
  through `internal/ui/teaexec`.

  way to detect that, so DevDesk does not try. There is no config key to turn the
  bar off (a future `app.terminal_progress: off` is a separate story if a terminal
  is found that prints the sequence). tmux needs `allow-passthrough` to forward it.

  `Failed N` (the context's remembered failures), the footer appends
  `· M stopping` to `N jobs running`, and the help has a "Terminal tab" section.

  the mapping, the fresh pointer, a measured scan, an open run, acknowledgement,
  scoping per context, a cancelled sync, that the bar does not change the content,
  and the two source guards; `terminal_progress_program_test.go` runs a real
  `tea.Program` and checks the bytes written (needs `mise run test-race`);
  `terminal_progress_text_test.go` the `:jobs` text.

  `T`), WSL inside Windows Terminal, tmux without `allow-passthrough` (nothing
  printed, tab unchanged), and a terminal without support such as Terminal.app or
  the Linux console (nothing printed). Open question: whether a full bar at 100 for
  Error and Warning reads right, or looks like completion.

Many terminals (Windows Terminal, for one) can show a progress bar on the tab or in the taskbar. DevDesk uses it to show the work of the current context:

- no bar when nothing runs;
- an indeterminate bar while a running job has no known size yet (a clone that is still listing repositories, or a run of a single target);

- orange while a stopped job has not settled yet;
